facts.text: Norwood’s name first appeared in 1870 when the Cincinnati Enquirer reported the old town of Sharpsburg had been renamed Norwood.
The United States Playing Card Company built a massive factory in Norwood in 1900, eventually becoming the world’s largest card manufacturer.
In 1809, Samuel Bowman bought land along what are now Montgomery Road and Smith/Carthage Avenue, laying the groundwork for Norwood’s early settlement.
Norwood’s historic Norwood Brick plant supplied clay bricks for many of Cincinnati’s landmark buildings in the late 19th century.
The Norwood Mound, an Adena earthwork, sits in the city and is listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
The city’s first industrial boom began when the Cincinnati, Lebanon and Northern railroad spurred subdivision construction in the early 20th century.
